items.stem:
The diagram shows the net of a cube.
The six faces are labelled A, B, C, D, E and F.
The net is folded to make the cube.

parts.t: Write down the letter of the face that is opposite face A.
Write down the letter of the face that is opposite face B.
Write down the letter of the face that is opposite face C.

sols: Squares that share an edge in the net become faces that meet along an edge of the cube, so they can never be opposite.
check pairs that are further apart
Fold the net keeping square A flat as the top of the cube: B folds down to become the right-hand face and C folds round to become the front face.
each square turns through 90° along the shared edge
D is joined to C and folds underneath, so the face opposite A is D
Continuing the fold, E is joined to D and becomes the left-hand face of the cube.
B is the right-hand face, so the face opposite B is E
Finally F is joined to E and becomes the back face.
C is the front face, so the face opposite C is F
Check: the three pairs A–D, B–E and C–F use all six faces exactly once ✓

items.stem:
The diagram shows the net of a solid prism.
The cross-section of the prism is a right-angled triangle with sides 3 cm and 4 cm, and the prism is 10 cm long.

parts.t: Write down the length of the third side of the triangle.
Work out the total surface area of the prism.
Calculate the volume of the prism.

sols: The triangle is right-angled with shorter sides 3 cm and 4 cm.
The net is two triangles and three rectangles.
the perimeter of the cross-section × the length

items.stem:
The diagram shows the net of a solid cylinder of radius 5 cm and height 12 cm.
The net is made from a rectangle and two circles.

parts.t:
Calculate the length of the rectangle.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Calculate the total surface area of the cylinder.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: When the rectangle is rolled up, its length becomes the circumference of the circular end.

items.stem:
The diagram shows the net of a solid pyramid with a square base of side 10 cm.
Each triangular face has a slant height of 13 cm, measured from the middle of a base edge.

parts.t: Work out the area of one triangular face.
Work out the total surface area of the pyramid.
Write down the number of edges of the pyramid.

sols: Each triangle has base 10 cm and perpendicular height 13 cm.
the slant height is the height of the triangular face
Base = 10 × 10 = 100 cm<sup>2</sup> and there are four triangles.
The square base has 4 edges and there are 4 sloping edges up to the apex.

items.stem:
The diagram shows the net of a solid.
It is made from six identical rectangles and two identical regular hexagons.

parts.t: Write down the mathematical name of the solid.
Write down the number of vertices of the solid.
Write down the number of edges of the solid.
Show that F + V − E = 2 for this solid, where F, V and E are the numbers of faces, vertices and edges.

ms:
B1
must show F = 8 and the correct substitution
sols: The two hexagons are the identical parallel ends and the six rectangles wrap around them.
a prism with a hexagonal cross-section
Each hexagon has 6 corners and there are two hexagonal ends.
6 edges on each hexagon and 6 edges joining the two hexagons.

items.stem:
An open box has no lid.
The base is a rectangle measuring 40 cm by 25 cm and the box is 15 cm deep.
The diagram shows the net of the box.

parts.t: Work out the area of card needed to make the box.

Card costs $0.0008 per square centimetre.
Work out the cost of the card for one box.

sols: The box has no lid, so the net is one base and four rectangular sides.

items.stem:
The diagram shows the net of a solid cone.
It is made from a sector of a circle of radius 10 cm and a circle of radius 6 cm.
[The curved surface area of a cone, A = πrl.]

parts.t: Show that the angle of the sector is 216°.

Calculate the curved surface area of the cone.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Calculate the total surface area of the cone.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

ms:
M1 for arc of sector = circumference of base, x⁄360 × 2 × π × 10 = 2 × π × 6 oe
A1 nfww
sols: When the net is folded, the arc of the sector becomes the circumference of the base circle.
This is the same as the sector area <sup>216</sup>⁄<sub>360</sub> × π × 10<sup>2</sup> = 60π ✓
the sector is the curved surface

items.stem:
A closed box is a cuboid with a square base of side x cm and height 3x cm.
The diagram shows the net of the box.

parts.t: Show that the total surface area of the box is 14x2 cm2.

The total surface area of the box is 350 cm2.
Find the value of x.
Calculate the volume of the box.

ms:
M1 for 14x2 = 350 or x2 = 25
A1 cao (positive root only)
sols: The net has two squares of side x and four rectangles x by 3x.
x is a length, so take the positive root

items.stem: The diagram shows three arrangements of six identical squares, A, B and C.

parts.t: Write down the letters of the arrangements that are nets of a cube.

ms:
B1 for each correct letter, with no incorrect letter
In B the 2 by 2 block folds two squares onto the same face
sols: A net of a cube must fold so that the six squares become six different faces.
A is the cross shape: the four squares in the row wrap round to make the sides and the two extra squares fold over to make the top and bottom ✓
B has a 2 by 2 block of squares. Folding the block, two of its squares would land on the same face, leaving one face uncovered ✗
no cube net contains a 2 by 2 block
C is a 1–4–1 arrangement with the single squares on opposite sides of the row of four ✓

items.stem: The diagram shows the net of a cube with edges of length 3 cm.

parts.t: Work out the perimeter of the net.
Work out the area of the net.

ms:
M1 for 14 edges counted or 14 × 3
A1 cao
sols: Count the edges of squares that lie on the outside of the net.
There are 14 outside edges, each 3 cm long.
6 squares have 24 edges altogether; the 5 joins each hide 2 edges: 24 − 10 = 14
the same as the surface area of the cube

items.stem:
An open box, with no lid, is a cube with edges of 12 cm.
The diagram shows the net of the box.

parts.t: Write down the number of faces of the open box.
Work out the area of card used to make the box.
Work out the volume of the box.

sols: A cube has 6 faces; the open box is missing its lid.
The box still holds the same as a 12 cm cube.

The rectangle measures 25.13 cm by 10 cm.

parts.t:
Calculate the radius of the cylinder.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Calculate the area of one circular end.

items.stem:
The diagram shows the net of a dice.
On a dice, the numbers on opposite faces add up to 7.
Three of the faces are numbered 1, 2 and 3.

parts.t: Find the value of x.
Find the value of y.
Find the value of z.

ms:
B1
face x is opposite the face numbered 3

B1
face y is opposite the face numbered 2

B1
face z is opposite the face numbered 1 (the middle of the strip)
sols: Squares that share an edge become adjacent faces, so opposite faces are two squares apart in the net.
Face x is above the middle square of the strip and the face numbered 3 is below it, so x and 3 are opposite.
top and bottom of the cube
In the strip of four, the 1st and 3rd squares are opposite: the face numbered 2 is opposite face y.
The 2nd and 4th squares of the strip are opposite: the face numbered 1 is opposite face z.
check: 1 to 6 are all used once ✓

items.stem:
The diagram shows the net of a closed cuboid.
The strip of four rectangles is 26 cm long altogether, the first rectangle is 5 cm wide and the height of the cuboid is 4 cm.

parts.t: Work out the length of the cuboid.
Work out the total surface area of the cuboid.
Work out the volume of the cuboid.

ms:
M1 for 2 × (5×8 + 5×4 + 8×4) or 26 × 4 + 2 × 5 × 8 oe
A1 FT their 8
sols: The strip is made of two 5 cm rectangles and two rectangles of the unknown length b.
opposite faces of a cuboid are identical
or the strip 26 × 4 = 104 plus the two 8 by 5 faces, 80

parts.t: Show that the total surface area of the cuboid is (48 + 20h) cm2.

The total surface area of the cuboid is 148 cm2.
Find the value of h.

sols: The net has two 6 by 4 rectangles, two 6 by h rectangles and two 4 by h rectangles.

items.stem: The diagram shows the net of a solid. It is made from four identical equilateral triangles with sides of 6 cm.

parts.t: Write down the mathematical name of the solid.
Write down the number of edges of the solid.

Calculate the total surface area of the solid.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

ms:
M1 for 4 × 1⁄2 × 6 × 6 × sin 60 oe, or one triangle = 15.58… seen
A1 (exact 36√3)
sols: Four triangular faces meeting at a point: the solid is a tetrahedron
The tetrahedron has 4 vertices, and every pair of vertices is joined by an edge.
Area of one equilateral triangle = <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub> × 6 × 6 × sin 60° = 15.588… cm<sup>2</sup>

The diagram shows the net of a solid prism of length 10 cm.
The cross-section is an equilateral triangle with sides of 6 cm.

parts.t:
Calculate the area of one triangular face.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Calculate the total surface area of the prism.
Calculate the volume of the prism.

sols: The triangle is equilateral, so the angle between two 6 cm sides is 60°.

items.stem:
The diagram shows the net of a solid pyramid with a square base of side 10 cm.
Each sloping edge of the pyramid is 13 cm long.

parts.t: Show that the perpendicular height of each triangular face is 12 cm.
Work out the total surface area of the pyramid.

ms:
M1 for 132 − 52 or 169 − 25 seen
A1 for √144 = 12 nfww

M1 for 102 + 4 × 1⁄2 × 10 × 12 or 100 + 240
A1 cao
M0 for using 13 as the height of the triangles (360)
sols: Each triangular face is isosceles: base 10 cm and equal sides 13 cm.
The perpendicular height splits it into two right-angled triangles with base 5 cm and hypotenuse 13 cm.

items.stem:
A rectangular paper label is wrapped once around the curved surface of a cylindrical tin of radius 3.5 cm and height 11 cm.
The label covers the whole height of the tin and its two ends overlap by 1 cm.

parts.t:
Calculate the length of the label.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Calculate the area of the label.

sols: Unrolled, the label is a rectangle whose length is the circumference plus the overlap.

items.stem:
The diagram shows the net of a solid.
It is made from a regular hexagon and six identical isosceles triangles.

parts.t: Write down the mathematical name of the solid.
Write down the number of faces of the solid.
Write down the number of vertices of the solid.
Work out the number of edges of the solid.

ms:
B1
accept pyramid with a hexagonal base

B1
6 round the base + the apex

B1
6 base edges + 6 sloping edges (or from F + V − 2)
sols: The six triangles fold up from the hexagon and meet at a point.
Vertices = 6 corners of the hexagon + 1 apex = 7
Edges = 6 round the hexagon + 6 sloping edges to the apex = 12

items.stem:
The diagram shows a sector of a circle of radius 9 cm with angle 240°.
The straight edges are joined together to make the curved surface of a cone.
[The volume, V, of a cone with radius r and height h is V = 1⁄3πr2h.]

parts.t: Show that the radius of the base of the cone is 6 cm.

Calculate the perpendicular height of the cone.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Calculate the volume of the cone.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

ms:
M1 for arc = 240⁄360 × 2 × π × 9 (= 12π = 37.7…)
A1 for 2πr = 12π leading to r = 6 nfww

M1 for 1⁄3 × π × 62 × their 6.708…
A1 FT their (b)
sols: The arc of the sector becomes the circumference of the base of the cone.
The radius of the sector, 9 cm, becomes the slant height of the cone.

items.stem:
The diagram shows the net of a cube. The faces are labelled A to F and some of the corners are labelled P, Q, R, S, T, U, V and W.
The net is folded to make the cube.

parts.t: Write down the letters of the two corners that meet corner P.
Write down the letter of the corner that meets corner Q.
Write down the edge of the net that is joined to the edge PQ.

ms:
B1 for each
fold A up from face C: P is above the left end of the strip

B2 for ST (or TS)
B1 FT for the edge joining their (a) and their (b) if these two corners are adjacent
sols: Keep face C as the base. Faces B, D, E and A fold up to become the four sides, and F folds up too.
P is the top-left corner of face A. When A folds up it stands above the corner where faces B, C and A meet.
Folding B up, its top-left corner R rises to the same top corner. Folding the strip round, E comes back to meet B, and its far corner T is that same corner.
the strip B–C–D–E wraps round to a closed band, so R and T meet
three squares meet at every corner of a cube
Q is the other top corner of face A. The band closes so that the top of D–E edge, corner S, is directly under it.
Edge PQ is the top edge of face A that is not attached to anything in the net.
P meets T and Q meets S, and S, T are the ends of the top edge of face E.
So edge PQ is joined to edge ST

items.stem:
A closed box is a cuboid with a square base of side x cm and height h cm.
The volume of the box is 500 cm3.
The box is made from a net cut from a single sheet of card.

parts.t: Write down an expression for h in terms of x.
Show that the total area of the net, A cm2, is given by A = 2x2 + 2000⁄x.
Calculate the value of A when x = 6, when x = 8 and when x = 10.
Which of these three values of x uses the least card? Write down the height of that box.

ms:
M1 for 2x2 + 4xh oe (2 squares + 4 rectangles)
A1 for substituting their h: 4x × 500⁄x2 = 2000⁄x nfww

B2 for all three (405.3…, 378, 400)
B1 for two correct
sols: The net is 2 squares of side x and 4 rectangles x by h.
